newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary restaurant bombing kills two Chinese women.
newsitem.headline: Hungary restaurant bombing kills two Chinese women.

text.p: A hand grenade exploded in a popular Chinese restaurant in Budapest, killing the owner's wife and daughter on Friday in the deadliest in a spate of bombings in the Hungarian capital, police said.

The two Chinese women, who were identified only as the owner's wife and daughter, were killed shortly after midnight when they entered the restroom where a Yugoslavian-made hand grenade had been planted, police said.
Other Chinese at the restaurant took the victims to a nearby military hospital where they were pronounced dead.
Police said the owner, identified only as a Mr Cheng, was in shock and they were seeking an interpreter to help question him.
The powerful explosion ripped the restroom door from its hinges. Blood and debris were smeared on the floor of The Great Wall Restaurant, near Heroes Square in a popular tourist area of the city.

Since last September, Budapest has been shaken by a dozen bombings and at least a half dozen shootings in an apparent gangland war. One known gangland figure was killed last year when he was shot dead at the wheel of his car.
Police said they could not say immediately who planted the hand grenade and said they did not know if the two women were the intended victims.
Earlier police had said the device was in a sack left in the rest room but they later said the circumstances were still under investigation.
"What we can say is that it was shortly after midnight, after the restaurant had closed, and there were no more guests in the restaurant," said police spokesman Andre Nagy.
"Since it was after closing time it means the attack was not aimed at the guests but against the owner or employees," he said. "It may have been a warning but against whom we don't know."
Dozens of Chinese from Budapest's 2,000-member Chinese community gathered in the restaurant to console the owner, who did not emerge to talk to reporters.
One young Chinese man, who declined to give his name, said as he entered the building: "I'm devastated. I have no idea why this happened."
In a separate incident, police said that a masked man threw petrol-filled Molotov cocktails through the window of a shoe store in a main commercial street on Thursday.
Store security personnel heard the glass being smashed and chased the man before he had time to set the two bombs alight, police said.
